what_breaks: A failed line save (quota) can show no visible error on a long order. The banner goes to the page region under the h1, not to the top of the line form panel. Focus then moves straight back to Save, so the browser scrolls away from the banner. The form looks as if Save did nothing.
evidence: Input: an order with about 20 lines (each row at least 2.75rem) and full storage. onSubmit line 277 commit fails, line 279 showBanner, main.js line 64 querySelector('[data-banner-region]') finds the only region, which sits under the h1 (order-view.js line 335); formHolder has none. main.js line 65 focuses the banner, then order-view.js line 280 ui.save.focus() scrolls back to the form after the total line, below all rows. UI-SPEC 7.6 says 'a failed save keeps the form open with a banner at the top of its panel'.

what_breaks: Deleting an order while a dirty line form is open asks 'Discard your changes?' after the delete has already happened. Keep editing leaves the deleted order on screen. Its Cancel then throws and shows APP-01; its Save line replaces the screen with not-found and drops the typed text.
evidence: Delete order is not disabled while the form is open (only addButton and the row buttons take ui.open, lines 74-75, 206). Input: open Add line, type 'x', Delete order, confirm. confirmDelete line 315 commits, line 320 location.replace('#/orders') does not clear state.form. main.js onHashChange line 184 sees form.isDirty() true and calls askToDiscard. onSafe line 175 restores the hash of the deleted order, and render is skipped because it equals renderedHash. Cancel: cancelForm, closeForm, drawLines line 205 currentOrder() is undefined, line 207 now.lines throws TypeError, APP-01.

what_breaks: Keep editing throws when focus was last on Save line or Cancel in the line form. The user gets APP-01 telling them to reload, and reloading loses the typed text. The normal R-21 path reaches this: a failed save, then leaving to delete data as the message advises.
evidence: Lines 217-219 store event.target.id on focusin, and Save line and Cancel have no id (components.js actionButton), so ui.lastFocused becomes ''. Line 280 ui.save.focus() sets this on every failed save. Input: dirty line form, failed save, click Orders, Keep editing. main.js line 176 calls restoreFocus, line 237 document.getElementById('') returns null, .focus() throws TypeError, the window error listener shows APP-01. The route forms guard this with 'lastFocused ? ... : ...'; the line form does not.

what_breaks: After a failed line save or Remove, a successful retry leaves the danger banner on screen. The page says 'so this was not saved' for a change that was saved.
evidence: Input: a Save line or Remove fails with STO-01, the user frees space, and the retry succeeds. Lines 283-284 (closeForm, addButton.focus) and lines 298-299 (drawLines, addButton.focus) touch only linesHolder, totalHolder and formHolder. Nothing empties the banner region created at line 335. UI-SPEC section 6: 'a banner leaves when its cause is gone'.

what_breaks: A newly saved customer does not appear in the list when an older search text is still active. The user lands on 'No customers match this search.' straight after saving.
evidence: Input: search 'zzz', open New customer, save 'Ana'. customer-form.js line 116 goes to #/customers, line 114 reads the retained state.searchCustomers, searchCustomers filters Ana out. ADR-005 line 46 keeps the text between screens on purpose, while R-01 says 'then the customer appears in the list'. The conflict between the two needs a decision.

what_breaks: Opening a route form puts focus on the h1, not on the first editable field.
evidence: render line 162 always calls h1.focus(), and renderCustomerForm and renderOrderForm return h1 (customer-form.js line 130, order-form.js line 220). UI-SPEC section 8: 'A route renders a form: the first editable field (customer form: Name; new order: Customer select, or Date when the customer is set; edit order: Date)'.

what_breaks: A storage failure on a route form moves focus to the banner, so Save is not ready for a retry. The same happens at order-form.js line 199. The line form handles this correctly at order-view.js line 280.
evidence: customer-form.js line 112 calls showBanner, and main.js line 65 ends in setBanner(...).focus(). UI-SPEC section 8: 'Failed Save, storage: stays on Save, ready to retry'.

what_breaks: Cancel on an Edit line form always sends focus to Add line, not to the Edit button that opened the form.
evidence: openForm line 232 stores the clicked Edit button, and line 235 drawLines rebuilds every row, which disconnects it. Line 253 then finds opener.isConnected false and uses addButton. UI-SPEC section 8: 'Cancel on the line form: the button that opened it'.

what_breaks: The no-lines state has no Add line button in its panel, and the h2 row still shows one, the reverse of the spec.
evidence: Lines 113-115 append only the paragraph, and line 199 always adds addButton to the h2 row. UI-SPEC 7.6: 'No lines yet. Add the first one. + Add line (primary), inside the table panel; the h2 row's Add line is not shown then'.

what_breaks: A document that passes the shape check can still make the screens throw. The user then gets APP-01 on a broken screen, not the R-20 error with its copy and start-empty exits.
evidence: Line 17 checks date only as text and isLine checks only isCount. Input 1: a stored order with date 'x': format.js line 14 new Date('xT00:00:00Z') is Invalid Date, format throws RangeError in order-list.js line 51. Input 2: quantity and unitPriceCents both 9007199254740991: money.js line 25 throws from toRow in listOrders. Only a damaged or hand-edited document reaches this, so a user cannot produce it through the app.

what_breaks: A zero-padded quantity longer than five digits is refused even though its value is in range.
evidence: QUANTITY_PATTERN is /^\d{1,5}$/, while ADR-007 line 15 says '^\d+$, then the range 1 to MAX_QUANTITY'. Input '000005' fails line 98 and returns line.quantity.invalid, yet the value is 5. '00005' passes. No test in tests/validation.test.js or tests/validation.spec.mjs uses this input.

what_breaks: Above about 7.04e15 cents, cents / 100 can no longer hold two exact decimals, so a shown total can be one cent off although addLine accepts it as safe. Reaching this takes about 7 000 maximum lines, so it is a theoretical limit.
evidence: From 2^46 the spacing of a double is 1/64, above 0.01. Settle with a test in tests/format.test.js: assert formatMoney(9007199254740991, 'en') equals '€90,071,992,547,409.91'.

what_breaks: If a browser reports a full quota under another name, it maps to 'unavailable', so the user sees STO-02 and not STO-01. Firefox has historically used NS_ERROR_DOM_QUOTA_REACHED. The STO-02 text still says deleting data frees space.
evidence: Line 52 tests only error.name === 'QuotaExceededError'. Settle with the manual check in docs/MANUAL-CHECKS.md line 57, run in Firefox: fill localStorage and read which code appears.

what_breaks: The blob URL is revoked in the same tick as link.click(), which some browsers may treat as cancelling the download, so Export data would do nothing with no error.
evidence: Lines 113-115 run link.click(), link.remove(), URL.revokeObjectURL(url) with no delay. Settle by running the R-29 manual check under the CSP in Safari and Firefox and confirming the file arrives.

what_breaks: crypto.randomUUID exists only in secure contexts. On a plain http address such as http://192.168.x.x:8000, every create throws TypeError and shows APP-01, so no customer can be added. localhost and GitHub Pages are not affected.
evidence: deps.newId at line 49 calls crypto.randomUUID() with no check, reached from createCustomer in customers.js line 19. Settle by opening the app through the machine's LAN IP and saving a customer.

what_breaks: No test covers years 0000 to 0099, so deleting the setUTCFullYear line would pass every test. Date.UTC then maps 0099 to 1999 and '0099-01-01', a real date, is refused.
evidence: tests/dates.spec.mjs line 23 accepts only 2026-02-28, 2024-02-29, 2000-02-29, 2026-12-31 and 2026-01-01. The title of tests/dates.test.js line 5 names only 2026-02-28 and 2024-02-29. The refusal list cannot catch this mutation, because the mutation only refuses more dates.

what_breaks: A stored order date is only checked to be a string, so a hand-edited document with an unparseable date passes as valid. The order screens then crash instead of showing the R-20 blocked screen. No copy way out is offered, Reload repeats the crash, and only Erase all data on the customer list stays reachable.
evidence: Input under invoice-app: {"version":1,"nextOrderNumber":2,"customers":[{"id":"c1","name":"A","email":"","phone":"","address":""}],"orders":[{"id":"o1","number":"ORD-0001","customerId":"c1","date":"not-a-date","notes":"","lines":[]}]}. isOrder (shape.js:17) sees a string, so load() returns ok:true and canWrite is true. format.js:14 builds new Date('not-a-dateT00:00:00Z'), an Invalid Date, and Intl.DateTimeFormat.format throws RangeError. Callers are order-list.js:51 (#/orders), customer-detail.js:69 (#/customers/c1) and order-view.js:30 (#/orders/o1). render() throws and the window error listener shows only APP-01 with Reload. The data model sketch types the field as YYYY-MM-DD, and shape.js checks number with a regex but not date. No test covers a malformed date string: storage.spec.mjs:204 only tries the number 5. Not reachable through the forms, because isRealDate guards them.

what_breaks: Stored quantity and unitPriceCents are only checked to be safe integers. A valid-looking document can make the line total unsafe, which throws on the order list, on that customer's detail and on the order view. The order and the customer then cannot be removed through their screens, the lock-out ADR-004 says the shape check must avoid; only Erase all data remains. Negative values also pass and show broken text.
evidence: Input: a line with "quantity":9007199254740991,"unitPriceCents":2. isCount passes both and load() returns ok:true. lineTotalCents gives about 1.8e16, requireSafeInteger throws (money.js:25), reached through orderTotalCents from toRow (orders.js:26) on #/orders, the search and the customer detail, and from order-view.js:91 and :171. The order view cannot render, so the line and the order cannot be removed through their screens, and the customer stays blocked by R-04. Only APP-01 appears, with no copy option. Separately, "unitPriceCents":-50 passes and priceInputText(-50) gives -1.-50 in the edit field (Math.floor gives -1, -50 % 100 gives -50). The accepted test at storage.spec.mjs:328 only uses 10000. Not reachable through the forms.

what_breaks: nextOrderNumber accepts any safe integer, including negative values and the maximum. Creating one order then writes a document the app itself refuses on the next load, so a readable data set becomes blocked as corrupt.
evidence: Input 1: "nextOrderNumber":-5 with no orders. orderNumber gives String(-5).padStart(4,'0'), so ORD-00-5, and save succeeds. On reload ORDER_NUMBER (/^ORD-(\d+)$/) fails, isOrder is false and load returns corrupt. Input 2: "nextOrderNumber":9007199254740991. createOrder (orders.js:44) stores 9007199254740992, isCount is false on reload, and load returns corrupt. ADR-004 says the counter starts at 1. Not reachable from a document the app wrote itself.

what_breaks: Order number uniqueness compares strings, so two orders with the same numeric number pass the shape check and R-06 uniqueness is not enforced on stored data.
evidence: Input: two orders with "number":"ORD-1" and "number":"ORD-0001" and "nextOrderNumber":2. allUnique sees two different strings, and orderNumberValue gives 1 for both, which is below 2, so the document is accepted and two orders show the same numeric sequence. Hand-edited data only.

what_breaks: Extra keys in a stored document are neither refused nor removed. They reach the domain, are written back on every save, and customer-level extras reach the R-29 export. ADR-004 fixes the document to the fields of the sketch with nothing added.
evidence: Input: a valid document plus "backup":[{"name":"Old customer","email":"old@example.com"}] at the root, or "nationalId":"123" on a customer. hasValidShape checks only the named fields. Rest destructuring at storage.js:22 keeps backup, every command spreads ...data, and save writes it back (storage.js:50), so deleting all orders and the customer leaves that personal data stored despite the R-04 text. export.js:11 clones the customer record whole, so nationalId lands in the export file. updateCustomer (customers.js:29) silently drops the same extra field. Hand-edited data only. No test feeds an extra key.

what_breaks: Stored ids are only checked to be strings, and routeToHash puts them into the hash without encoding. Some records then cannot be opened, or open the wrong screen. The value stays inside the fragment, so it cannot become a script URL.
evidence: Input: customer "id":"" gives href #/customers/, and parseRoute (router.js:41) refuses an empty part, so not-found. "id":"new" gives #/customers/new, which opens the new customer form instead of the record. "id":"a b" gives location.hash #/customers/a%20b, parseRoute does not decode it, the find fails, so not-found. Line "id":"": openForm('', button) in order-view.js:229 treats it as no line and opens Add instead of Edit. The record cannot be deleted through its screen. Hand-edited data only.

what_breaks: Text made only of invisible characters passes the required-field checks, because trim() does not remove them. A customer or line can be saved with no visible name or description. Direction override characters can also make one name look like another, despite the A-12 goal of telling customers apart.
evidence: Input: paste U+200B (zero width space) as the name. U+200B is not ECMAScript whitespace, so textOf keeps it, length is 1, lengthError passes, and createCustomer stores it. The list row at customer-list.js:32 has a link with no visible text. The same path applies to the line description (validation.js:105, 109). Literally this meets R-01 (1 to 100 characters after trimming), so it is advisory. Whether invisible-only text counts as empty is a decision for the human. No test covers it.

what_breaks: save() has no check of its own, so a malformed value overwrites good data. The write lock only guards the load state. The spread also runs after version, so a version key in data replaces the constant. Validation of the document lives only in the callers.
evidence: Direct call: save({}) writes {"version":1} over the stored document, and the next load is corrupt. save({version:2,...}) writes version 2 because ...data comes after version: VERSION, and the next load is newer. No reachable caller found: commit() receives only result.data from a successful domain command, and parseDocument strips version. Probe that settles it: a storage test that calls save after a good load with a value lacking customers, and one with a version key.

what_breaks: Quota detection depends on the exact error name. A browser that reports quota under another name gets STO-02 instead of STO-01, so the message differs while the failure stays visible and the data stays safe.
evidence: Only name === 'QuotaExceededError' maps to quota. Older Firefox used NS_ERROR_DOM_QUOTA_REACHED, which I could not confirm for current versions. Tests use only a fake DOMException with the standard name. Probe that settles it: the manual R-21 check of S11, run in current Firefox and Safari, confirming STO-01 appears.

what_breaks: CI actions are referenced by a moving major tag, so the code that runs in the pipeline can change without a commit here. The kit checkout is pinned by SHA, but the actions themselves are not.
evidence: gate.yml:15 and :20 use actions/checkout@v7, gate.yml:27 uses actions/setup-node@v7, and node-version is 22 with no exact version. DR-04 requires pinning by commit SHA, digest or exact version. The impact is limited because permissions are contents: read and persist-credentials is false.

what_breaks: The quantity rule differs from ADR-007, which says ^\d+$ then the range. Leading zeros that give a valid value are refused at six digits or more, but accepted at five or fewer.
evidence: Input 000001: QUANTITY_PATTERN /^\d{1,5}$/ fails, so the app shows the quantity error, though the value is 1. Input 00001 is accepted as 1. This is the only effect. Very long digit strings are refused either way, and no invalid value is stored.

what_breaks: parseDocument rethrows any JSON.parse error that is not a SyntaxError, so load() can throw instead of returning a result. start() calls load() before it registers the error listeners, so such a throw leaves an empty page with no message. Writing stays locked, so no data is lost, but the failure is not visible.
evidence: storage.js:15 rethrows, and createStorage.load has no try around parseDocument (storage.js:42). main.js:189 calls storage.load() while the error and unhandledrejection listeners are only added at main.js:197 and :198. No trigger found: it needs an engine error from JSON.parse, such as an out-of-memory error on a very large stored text. Probe that settles it: a storage test with a backing store whose text makes JSON.parse throw a non-SyntaxError, or a manual check in each target browser with a stored document near the quota.

what_breaks: The Blob URL is revoked in the same task as link.click(). A browser that starts the download later could fail it, so the R-29 export would not arrive while the app shows no error.
evidence: downloadExport calls link.click() at customer-detail.js:113 and URL.revokeObjectURL(url) at :115 with nothing in between that waits. Not shown to fail in any current browser. Probe that settles it: the R-29 line of docs/MANUAL-CHECKS.md, run in current Firefox and Safari as well as Chromium, confirming the file arrives with its full content.

what_breaks: S7's builder tests hold only part of the plan's Tests first list. 12 of the 18 titles are missing from tests/storage.test.js and tests/shape.test.js. No rule is lost, because the same titles exist in tests/storage.spec.mjs, so the tester's specs are the only cover for them.
evidence: PLAN S7 step 1: 'Write the tests above'. Missing from the builder files, among others: `R-20 save after a corrupt or newer load answers blocked and leaves the stored text unchanged`, `R-21 any other setItem error answers unavailable and leaves the old text`, `R-21 openBrowserStorage answers unavailable on every call when the access to localStorage throws`, `R-32 a removeItem that throws answers unavailable`. tests/storage.test.js has 5 tests. Line 28 `R-21 a setItem that throws QuotaExceededError answers quota` also drops the plan's 'and leaves the old text' assertion. The storage.spec.mjs lines 335, 407, 446 and 507 carry these rules.

what_breaks: Four S5 plan tests are missing from the builder's file. They exist only in tests/lines.spec.mjs.
evidence: PLAN S5 Tests first lists `R-11 addLine keeps the lines in the order they were added`, `R-12 updateLine with an invalid price returns the errors and no data`, `R-13 removeLine of the only line leaves an order that totals 0`, `R-15 updateLine returns line.total.too-large on unitPrice when the new order total is not a safe integer`. tests/lines.test.js has 6 tests and none of these. tests/lines.spec.mjs lines 66, 148, 186 and 229 hold them.

what_breaks: S3 and S6 builder tests merge or loosen plan titles, and only the specs hold the plan's strength. The merged R-05 test uses data where the compare order equals insertion order, so it does not prove the plan's sort rule. The export test checks only a fragment of A-13 and A-14.
evidence: PLAN S3: `R-05 searchCustomers returns its matches in the order of the compare function it is given` has no builder test; tests/customers.test.js:67 `R-05 searchCustomers trims, ignores case, matches name or email only` asserts ['c1','c2'] on data already in that order. PLAN S6: `R-29 buildCustomerExport states the purpose of A-13, the retention of A-14 and the currency EUR`; tests/export.test.js:19-20 asserts only `endsWith('The data is used for nothing else.')` and `includes('there is no fixed period')`. tests/customers.spec.mjs:234 and tests/export.spec.mjs:77-92 hold the stronger checks.

what_breaks: Production deps carry `now`, while ADR-003 and the tests use `today`. Every domain test fakes a dependency the app never supplies, and the plan's 'does not substitute deps.today' test guards a key that is absent in production.
evidence: ADR-003: '`deps` carries what the outside supplies, `newId` and `today`'. Code: `const deps = { newId: () => crypto.randomUUID(), now: () => Date.now() };`. tests/orders.test.js:5 `const deps = { newId: () => 'new-order', today: '2026-10-30' };`. src/ui/views/order-form.js:158 calls `todayIso(deps.now)` from the view.

what_breaks: Three views read the browser locale themselves instead of receiving it from the composition root, so the locale is not set in one place.
evidence: ADR-006: 'The locale is `navigator.language`, read once in `src/ui/main.js` and passed as an argument'. ADR-003: main.js alone 'supplies ... `navigator.language`, and hands them on as parameters'. Code: `const locale = navigator.language;` at customer-detail.js:135, order-list.js:105 and order-view.js:191.

what_breaks: Views do not have the ADR-003 shape: they get one context object holding the whole mutable state, and they attach several listeners instead of one delegated listener per container.
evidence: ADR-003: 'A view has the shape `render(container, viewModel, actions)` and one delegated listener per container (JS-11)'. Code: `export function renderOrderView(container, context)`; `for (const part of [linesRow, linesHolder, formHolder]) part.addEventListener('click', onClick);`; deleteButton has its own listener at order-view.js:323. customer-list.js:65 and :73 attach per-button listeners. Views also write `state.form` and `state.searchCustomers` directly.

what_breaks: `commit` only saves and swaps state. Each view does its own navigation and re-render, so the one write path of ADR-003 is split across seven call sites.
evidence: ADR-003: '`commit` calls `storage.save(result.data)`; only when that succeeds does it replace the state, navigate and render.' Code: `function commit(nextData) { ... state.data = nextData; return { ok: true }; }`. Navigation is in the views, for example customer-form.js:116 `location.hash = where.saved;`.

what_breaks: The code table is split in two: STO-03, STO-04 and the load-time STO-02 text live in the view, not in the one frozen object of main.js.
evidence: ADR-007, on the table with STO-01 to STO-05 and APP-01: 'The table lives in one frozen object in `src/ui/main.js`.' Code: blocked.js:3 `const TEXTS = Object.freeze({ corrupt: {...(STO-03)}, newer: {...(STO-04)}, unavailable: {...(STO-02)} })`. main.js:15 CODES holds only STO-01, STO-02, STO-05 and APP-01. UI-SPEC section 6 line 139 places these messages on the blocked screen, so the two documents may differ.

what_breaks: formatMoney adds an option the accepted decision does not list.
evidence: ADR-006: 'using `Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: 'currency', currency: CURRENCY })`'. Code adds `currencyDisplay: 'narrowSymbol',`.

what_breaks: formatDate parses an ISO string instead of building the date from Date.UTC as the decision says. The displayed day is the same; only the wording of the decision is not followed.
evidence: ADR-007: 'Dates are displayed through `formatDate(isoDate, locale)` in `src/ui/format.js`, built with `Date.UTC`'. Code: `formatter.format(new Date(`${isoDate}T00:00:00Z`))`.

what_breaks: The quantity pattern is narrower than the decision: `000001` is refused though its value is 1, which is in range under ADR-007.
evidence: ADR-007: 'Quantity is trimmed text matching `^\d+$`, then the range 1 to `MAX_QUANTITY`'. Code: `const QUANTITY_PATTERN = /^\d{1,5}$/;`.

what_breaks: routeToHash silently turns not-found into the customer list. No requirement, ADR or plan step asks for this, and the app's only caller is a test.
evidence: Code: `'not-found': () => '#/customers',`. ADR-005 lists nine routes and no hash for not-found. Used at tests/router.test.js:41. What would settle it: whether the human wants this default or the entry removed.

what_breaks: The S3 commit message uses a range instead of naming its IDs, so a search of the history for R-03, R-04 or R-05 misses it.
evidence: AGENTS.md rule 8: `S<n>: <what changed> (R-xx, R-yy)`. PLAN S3 Covers: 'R-01, R-02, R-03, R-04, R-05, R-06'. Commit bd4ef79: `S3: customer commands, list, search and label (R-01..R-06)`.

what_breaks: S8 added only one of the ten UX checks its plan section lists.
evidence: PLAN S8 Verify lists 10 `- [ ] UX:` lines, from 'keyboard only' to 'each screen of the slice matches its sketch'. MANUAL-CHECKS.md section S8 (lines 3-6) has only `- [ ] UX: keyboard only, from the first field to the outcome, focus visible at every step`. Commit 7ade51f added 6 lines.

what_breaks: S11 dropped its two screen checks, including the one S9 defers to S11. The first real test of the leave-a-form guard is on no list.
evidence: PLAN S11 lists `UX: customer form: Save with a bad email and an empty name, both errors show, focus lands on Name, nothing is saved` and `UX: leaving a form: type in a form, click Orders, then Keep editing: the text is still there; repeat with the browser's Back`. MANUAL-CHECKS.md section S11 ends at line 68 with neither. Line 28 says 'S11 completes this check with the first real form'.

what_breaks: S13's screen check is missing, so 'Back from an order keeps the search' is on no list.
evidence: PLAN S13 lists `UX: order list: with no customers only the "Add a customer first" message shows; with customers, Back from an order keeps the search`. MANUAL-CHECKS.md section S13 ends at line 167 without it.

what_breaks: The no-lines empty state has no Add line button in the panel, and the top Add line stays. The manual check was reworded to fit this.
evidence: UI-SPEC 7.6: 'Empty state: `No lines yet. Add the first one.` + `Add line` (primary), inside the table panel; the h2 row's `Add line` is not shown then'. Code: `const empty = element('div', 'empty-state'); empty.append(element('p', '', 'No lines yet. Add the first one.'));`; line 199 `linesRow.append(element('h2', '', 'Lines'), addButton);` is unconditional. PLAN S16: `R-18: from the no-lines message, Add line opens the form`; MANUAL-CHECKS.md:116 says `R-18: with no lines, the message shows and Add line opens the form`.

what_breaks: The row being edited still shows its disabled Edit and Remove buttons instead of the text Editing.
evidence: UI-SPEC section 6: 'Row being edited: `--color-info-bg` and the text `Editing` as its action cell.' Code: `actionsCell.append(rowActions(line, position, ui.open));` for every row. The word `Editing` does not appear in order-view.js.

what_breaks: On desktop the line form stacks Quantity and Unit price instead of placing them side by side.
evidence: UI-SPEC 7.6: 'Desktop: Description full width, then Quantity and Unit price side by side, gap `--space-4`, buttons in one row.' Code: `form.append(field(... 'line-description' ...), field(... 'line-quantity' ...), field(... 'line-unitPrice' ...), buttons);` with no `.form-pair` wrapper, the class customer-form.js:39 uses for this.

what_breaks: An unknown id shows the not-found screen, but with the title of the record screen and a nav item marked current.
evidence: UI-SPEC 7.7 serves 'any other hash, or an unknown `id`' with 'Page title: `Not found - Invoice app`'. Section 6: `Customers` is current 'neither on the not-found screen'. Code: `const route = SCREENS[parsed.name] ? parsed : { name: 'not-found' };` then markNav and routeTitle run on the parsed route, and only afterwards customer-detail.js:134 does `return renderNotFound(container)`. For `#/customers/x` the title is `Customer - Invoice app` and Customers stays current. MANUAL-CHECKS.md:15 expects 'the nav shows no current item'.

what_breaks: Opening a route form puts focus on the h1, not on the first editable field, so a keyboard user must tab in.
evidence: UI-SPEC section 8: 'A route renders a form | the first editable field (customer form: Name; new order: Customer select, or Date when the customer is set; edit order: Date)'. Code: `const h1 = state.blocked ? renderBlockedScreen() : renderRoute(); h1.focus();`, and customer-form.js:130 and order-form.js:220 both `return h1;`.

what_breaks: After a failed storage save on a route form, focus moves to the banner instead of staying on Save for a retry.
evidence: UI-SPEC section 8: 'Failed Save, storage | stays on Save, ready to retry; the banner has `role="alert"`'. Code: `showBanner(saved.code);` here and at order-form.js:199, and main.js:65 does `return setBanner(region, bannerFor(code)).focus();`. order-view.js:280 restores focus with `ui.save.focus()`; these two forms do not.

what_breaks: A failed line save puts the banner in the page region above the details, not at the top of the line form. With focus on Save lower down the page, the error can be off screen on a long order.
evidence: UI-SPEC section 6: 'with a form open, a banner goes at the top of that form's panel'. UI-SPEC 7.6: 'a failed save keeps the form open with a banner at the top of its panel (R-21)'. Code: `showBanner(saved.code);` finds the first `[data-banner-region]` (main.js:64), the one added at order-view.js:335. `lineForm` (lines 136-154) builds no region.

what_breaks: After a failed line save or Remove, a successful retry leaves the 'so this was not saved' banner on screen although the change was saved.
evidence: UI-SPEC section 6: 'a banner leaves when its cause is gone or the user moves to another screen'. Code: on success `closeForm(); addButton.focus();`, and `removeOne` does `drawLines(); addButton.focus();`. Neither clears the region, and neither `closeForm` nor `drawLines` touches it.

what_breaks: In stacked rows a real email is shown in normal text color, not muted.
evidence: UI-SPEC 7.1: 'Stacked rows: name in `--weight-bold`, email under it in `--color-text-muted`.' Code: `cell('td', 'cell', hasEmail ? 'cell-email' : 'cell-email cell-muted')`. styles.css has no rule for `.cell-email`.

what_breaks: Row links look like plain bold text at every width instead of links.
evidence: UI-SPEC section 6: 'the first cell holds an `<a>` styled as a link'; section 3 gives `--color-primary` to links. Code: `.row-open { color: var(--color-text); font-weight: var(--weight-bold); text-decoration: none; ...}`. 7.1 asks for `--weight-bold` only on stacked rows.

what_breaks: Two motions of the spec are missing: the button press has no duration, and the dialog backdrop does not fade.
evidence: UI-SPEC section 9: 'Button active: `transform` to `translateY(var(--press-offset))` over `--duration-fast`' and 'The dialog and its backdrop: `opacity` from 0 to 1 over `--duration-base`.' Code: `.button:active { transform: translateY(var(--press-offset)); }` with no `transition` anywhere in styles.css. `--duration-fast` is used only in `:root`. Line 366 `dialog::backdrop { background: var(--color-backdrop); }` has no animation.

what_breaks: Read-only inputs change border color on focus.
evidence: UI-SPEC section 6: 'Read-only (`readonly`): `--color-bg` fill, `--color-text`, no focus border change, ring still shown.' Code: `input:focus, select:focus, textarea:focus { border-color: var(--color-primary); }`, and line 316 `[readonly] { background: var(--color-bg); }` does not exclude it.

what_breaks: The sticky table header may not stick to the page, because every table panel has `overflow: hidden`.
evidence: UI-SPEC section 6: 'from 64rem `position: sticky`, `top: 0`, `z-index: 1`'. Code: `.panel-table { padding: 0; gap: 0; overflow: hidden; }` around `thead { position: sticky; ...}`. What would settle it: scroll a long list at desktop width in a browser.

what_breaks: A raw size sits outside `:root`, which the design-token check forbids.
evidence: UI-SPEC header: 'A value that is not here is a `NEEDS HUMAN`, not a guess.' MANUAL-CHECKS.md:24: 'no raw color, size or spacing outside :root in styles.css'. Code: `.banner-text { flex: 1 1 12rem; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }`.

what_breaks: Deleting a customer does not clear the in-memory search text. A name typed to find that customer stays on screen after the deletion, until a reload. Erase all data does clear it.
evidence: Rule: LD-07 'The person can have their personal data erased'; the reviewer question asks whether a delete leaves a copy 'in a cache or in an index'. Code: confirmDelete in customer-detail.js commits and then calls location.replace('#/customers'), with no reset of state.searchCustomers or state.searchOrders. Those resets exist only in eraseAll, src/ui/main.js:125-126. customer-list.js buildSearch does input.value = state.searchCustomers. Path: with at least two customers, type 'Jane' in the customer search, open Jane, press Delete customer and confirm. The list comes back with 'Jane' in the search box, and the R-04 banner had promised that all of this customer's data is erased. Limits: memory only, nothing is written to localStorage, and a reload clears it.

what_breaks: The export given to a person states purpose and retention in project-internal wording, including requirement ids the person cannot look up.
evidence: Rule: LD-06 'The person can obtain a copy of their personal data', and its Why asks for 'which data is held, for what purpose, how long'. Code: RETENTION reads 'the user applies this rule with R-04 and R-08. No legal retention applies while the app issues no invoices (A-10).' PURPOSE on line 3 carries backticked field names and an instruction to the app user ('should not hold details about other people'). Reading A: ADR-007 says these are 'frozen texts taken from A-13 and A-14' and R-29 asks the file to state them, so the text is compliant. Reading B: R-29 also says 'the user can answer a person's access request with this one file', and the recipient has no access to docs/REQUIREMENTS.md, so 'R-04', 'R-08' and 'A-10' tell them nothing. The human decides which reading holds.

what_breaks: A-13 says neither notes nor line description should hold details about other people, but the app warns only on notes. A person named in a line of another customer's order stays stored after that person is erased.
evidence: Rule: LD-03 'The app stores only the personal data its purpose needs, by default'. A-13: '`notes` and line `description` record what the order is about and should not hold details about other people'. Code: order-form.js:8 NOTES_HELPER says 'Keep details about other people out of this field.' The line-description field at order-view.js:147 has no helper, while the unit price field on the same form does. Reading A: UI-SPEC line 432, approved, gives the Description helper as 'none', so the build matches the spec. Reading B: the safeguard A-13 states for both fields reaches only one, and the R-04 banner text 'all of this customer's data is erased' does not cover such free text. Settled by the human saying whether the UI-SPEC row stands.

what_breaks: Order customerId is listed as personal data but cannot be corrected in place. An order saved on the wrong customer can only be deleted and rebuilt, which also uses up its number.
evidence: Rule: LD-04 'Personal data can be corrected, and the correction reaches every place it is shown'. REQUIREMENTS data model: 'Personal data: Customer id, name, email, phone, address; Order customerId, notes'. Code: validateOrderEdit in src/domain/validation.js takes date and notes only, and order-form.js:73 says 'To move an order, delete it and create a new one.' Path: A-12 allows two customers with the same name; the user picks the wrong one, adds lines, then notices. Reading A: A-06, confirmed by the human, makes delete and re-create the accepted correction path, so LD-04 is met. Reading B: the correction needs every line retyped and burns the order number (R-06), so the field cannot in fact be rectified 'without undue delay'. The requirements legal review (LEG-1 to LEG-11) did not weigh A-06 against LD-04. Settled by the human confirming A-06 under LD-04.

what_breaks: The accepted answer to threat T-02 (other sites on the shared github.io origin can read the key) rests on a runbook that does not exist. The app's own note says nothing about it.
evidence: Rule: LD-09 'Personal data does not leak into logs, error messages, URLs or the storage of a shared machine'. ADR-008 Answered: 'anyone who keeps real customer data runs the app from localhost or from an origin of their own. The runbook says so.' Check: docs/ has no RUNBOOK.md, .github/workflows holds only gate.yml, and docs/PLAN.md contains neither 'RUNBOOK' nor 'Pages', so no slice adds it. src/ui/views/customer-list.js:5 tells the user 'Your data lives only in this browser', with no word about the shared origin. No Pages workflow exists, so no user can reach this today. Settled by confirming the devops role writes the runbook line before the first publish, and by the human saying whether the published app itself must also show the demo-only warning.

what_breaks: The R-31 clause that search text stays out of the URL and page title has no test and no manual check. The code is correct today, but nothing would catch a regression.
evidence: Rule: LD-09, reviewer question 'Is there a test per rule the slice touches whose assertion fails if the rule is broken?'. R-31: 'the page title and the URL never contain ... the text typed into a search'. tests/router.test.js has 'R-31 parseRoute keeps no text of an unknown hash in its result' and 'R-31 the title of every route comes from the frozen table and holds no id', and neither involves search text. No R-31 title under tests/ mentions search. docs/MANUAL-CHECKS.md lists R-31 only at lines 5 and 16 (made-up id, unknown hash); neither types into a search box. Search state lives in src/ui/main.js and cannot run under Node (ADR-001), so a manual check is the available cover. Current code has no leak: searches stay in state.searchCustomers and state.searchOrders and never reach location or document.title.

what_breaks: The workflow uses two third-party GitHub actions that no decision names with an SPDX identifier, although ADR-001 says the project has no development dependencies.
evidence: Rule: LL-01 'Every third-party component is named with its SPDX licence identifier'. Code: gate.yml lines 15 and 20 'uses: actions/checkout@v7', line 27 'uses: actions/setup-node@v7'. A search of docs/ and AGENTS.md finds no mention of either. ADR-001: 'Dependencies: none, neither runtime nor development'. The second checkout fetches ioanbitza/sdlc, which is MIT and copyright Ioan Bita, so it is not third-party. Limits: the actions run only in CI and are not shipped, so no redistribution notice is owed, and A-15 names only 'library, font, icon set or adapted design'. Settled by the human saying whether CI actions count as components under LL-01. If they do, a decision names them with their SPDX ids, read from each action's own repository.
